conventions: TypeScript strict, ESM. Prettier 2.6 with the repo config (double quotes, trailing commas, 80 columns); eslint runs with --max-warnings=0, so an import-order warning fails the check.
Import order: externals, then @excalidraw/** packages, then relative imports; `import type` statements are separate and come after the value imports of the same group.

Inside packages/excalidraw import by relative path to the specific module; never from the barrel (`@excalidraw/excalidraw`, `..`, `../index`) except for types. excalidraw-app imports from `@excalidraw/excalidraw`, `@excalidraw/element` and `@excalidraw/common`.

Package layering: common is lowest, then element, then excalidraw, then excalidraw-app. A lower package never imports a value from a higher one; packages/element/src/pages.ts declares its own structural parameter types instead of importing AppState.

Components are function components written `export const Name = (...) =>` with props typed inline; a component's stylesheet sits beside it as global SCSS nested under `.excalidraw`, starting with `@use "../css/variables.module" as *;`.
User-facing strings go through `t("pages.x")` and into packages/excalidraw/locales/en.json only. Page names are document data, not UI strings: the default name is the literal `Page N`.

New DOM or browser API use goes through `app.ownerDocument` and `app.ownerWindow`, not the globals. To override properties of an existing type use `Merge<Base, Overrides>` from @excalidraw/common/utility-types, not `Omit<...> & Overrides`.

Immutable data: every write to a page list returns a new array of new records; never mutate an `ExcalidrawPage`. The only in-place element write this change adds is `adoptElementsIntoPage`, which Scene runs on elements it is taking ownership of, like `syncInvalidIndices` does.

Tests are Vitest with `globals: true`: describe, it and expect are not imported, `vi` is. Editor tests `render(<Excalidraw />)` from tests/test-utils and drive it with `API`, `Keyboard`, `Pointer`, `UI` from tests/helpers and the `window.h` hook. No new test dependency and no browser runner.

App-side helper classes follow App.selection.ts and App.clipboard.ts: `export class AppX { constructor(private app: App, private dependencies: {...}) {} }`, with arrow-function members, instantiated as a field of App.
Hot-path rule: a drawing with one page pays only a constant-time check per render. Page grouping runs when the scene is written or the page switches, never in render.

decisions.choice: A `pageId` field on the element in one flat element list, not separate element arrays per page. An older client or library that opens a multi-page file or room keeps `pageId` (restore spreads unknown props), ignores `appState.pages`, and shows every page's elements overlapped on one canvas; if it saves a file the page list is lost, and a new client then restores that file onto one default page (FR-20, FR-21). In a mixed room an older client's new elements have no `pageId`, so they land on the default page, and when the default page is tombstoned they are deleted by delete-wins.
rejected: Separate element arrays per page: every element-level path (Portal.broadcastScene, reconcileElements, getSceneVersion, Firebase storage, ElementsDelta) would need a per-page form, and the file's top-level `elements` would stop being the whole drawing for older readers
decisions.reason: reconciliation stays per element by version and nonce, one payload carries every page, and file, local storage and collaboration formats stay additive (NFR-1).

decisions.choice: An element with no `pageId` is on the page with id DEFAULT_PAGE_ID ("default"), and elements on that page never carry the field: restore and adoption delete it. Only elements on other pages have `pageId`. The default page record is a constant from `getDefaultPage()` (id default, name `Page 1`, index a0, version 1, nonce 0, updated 0).
rejected: Stamping every element: rewrites every element snapshot and changes every saved element, for no behaviour
A random default page id: two clients opening a legacy room would disagree on the page list
decisions.reason: one-page drawings stay byte-identical at element level, and clients converge on legacy rooms with no page data.

decisions.choice: Scene's existing getters and `replaceAllElements` are the active page: everything in App, actions, frames, selection, hit-testing, binding and the renderer sees only that page, and `replaceAllElements` adopts whatever it is given into the active page, which is how paste, library, Mermaid and drawing satisfy FR-16 with no site changes. Other pages are parked in `Scene.elementsByPage`. New `getAllElementsIncludingDeleted`, `getPageElements`, `replaceElementsByPage` and `setActivePage` are the only whole-drawing surface. Paging is opt-in with `new Scene(null, { paged: true })`: App's Scene sets it, and the temporary Scenes in delta.ts and transform.ts must never adopt.
rejected: Scene getters returning every page and each caller filtering: leaks through every action that reads its `elements` argument (select all, clear canvas, z-index, align)
decisions.reason: FR-14, FR-15 and FR-16 hold by construction instead of by auditing about 200 call sites.

decisions.choice: An index is only compared with elements of the same page. packages/element/src/fractionalIndex.ts does not change. The two whole-drawing paths group first: `restoreElements` restores page by page, and `reconcileElements` orders, validates and syncs each page group. Indices may repeat across pages. An older client that de-duplicates across pages keeps each page's relative order, because the order by (index, id) restricted to a page is that page's order.
rejected: One globally unique index order: every z-index, delta and insert path computes indices from the active page alone, so it would need all pages in context
decisions.reason: NFR-8 holds with the existing validators, which only ever see one page.

decisions.choice: Three AppState keys. `pages` (all records including tombstones, {browser,export,server} all true), `activePageId` ({browser,export} true, server false) and `pageViewports` ({browser,export} true, server false). Viewport is a separate key so that the record that syncs in collaboration can never carry one. The active page's viewport lives in scrollX, scrollY and zoom; `pageViewports` is written for a page when it is left, and refreshed for the active page by `getPageViewportsForSave` at serialize time. None of the three is in ObservedAppState, so page changes are never undoable.
rejected: Pages held only in Scene: `onChange`, `serializeAsJSON` and hosts that persist appState would all need a new parameter
decisions.reason: every pipeline that already carries appState (file, local storage, share link, onChange, initialData) gets pages with no signature change.

decisions.choice: Only AppPages and a result with `replaceDrawing: true` may change the three page keys. `syncActionResult` keeps prevAppState's values otherwise, and `updateScene` drops them from `sceneData.appState`, because most actions return a spread of a possibly stale appState and actionClearCanvas spreads getDefaultAppState.
rejected: Detecting change by reference: a stale async action would read as a drawing replacement
decisions.reason: a stale appState can't desync Scene from AppState or wipe the page list.

decisions.choice: ExcalidrawPage is {id, name, index, version, versionNonce, isDeleted, updated}. Order is the fractional `index`, ties broken by id. `reconcilePages` merges by id: a tombstone beats everything, otherwise higher version wins, then lower versionNonce, matching shouldDiscardRemoteElement. Records are bumped on every change. The pristine default record held by only one side is dropped when the other side is non-empty, so a joiner's fresh editor can't resurrect a default page whose tombstone expired. If no live record remains, the lowest record is revived, so clients always hold a page.
rejected: Whole-list last-write-wins: a concurrent create would lose one side's page
decisions.reason: the same version and nonce rule as elements gives FR-24 and FR-27 with no server logic.

decisions.choice: A page delete tombstones the record and marks its elements deleted. `applyPageTombstones` runs after every reconcile and marks any non-deleted element on a tombstoned page deleted, so a concurrent edit that arrives with a higher version still loses (FR-27). Tombstones sync while `updated` is within DELETED_ELEMENT_TIMEOUT, the same retention as deleted elements. `serializeAsJSON` strips tombstones so deleted page names never reach a file or share link.
decisions.reason: convergence with no server, and the rule is one pure function shared by Collab and Firebase.

decisions.choice: Store and History stay single-page and see only the active page; ElementsDelta, HistoryDelta, actionHistory and applyDeltas do not change. History keeps a stack pair per page behind `undoStack`/`redoStack` getters. On a switch, in-progress work is committed first so it lands on the leaving page, then `Store.resetSnapshot` re-seeds the snapshot from the target page with no increment. Remote changes to parked pages never reach the Store, so `onIncrement` describes the active page only, and that is documented.
rejected: Store over all pages with one global snapshot: History.perform would have to hand every page through actionHistory, and a page's deltas would mix with remote changes to other pages
decisions.reason: FR-17 needs per-page stacks and nothing else from history.

decisions.choice: `getSceneElements` and `getSceneElementsIncludingDeleted` stay the active page; new `getAllPagesElementsIncludingDeleted` is the drawing, and `onChange`'s elements argument is the whole drawing so a host that persists onChange keeps every page. `updateScene({ elements })` without `pages` routes each element: an explicit `pageId` naming a live page stays there, a known id stays on its page, anything else goes to the active page, and it replaces only the pages elements land on (an empty array clears the active page). `updateScene({ elements, pages })` is a whole-drawing write that replaces exactly: pages with no incoming elements become empty. One live page and no parked elements takes today's `replaceAllElements` path unchanged.
rejected: `getSceneElements*` returning every page: `exportScene` and canvas inspection by hosts would see pages that aren't on screen
decisions.reason: FR-16 and FR-29: page-ignoring hosts keep working, and a host writing back what onChange gave it can't collapse pages onto the active page.

decisions.choice: `VERSIONS.excalidraw` stays 2. Pages travel as `appState.pages`, `appState.activePageId` and `appState.pageViewports`, elements as `pageId`. `restoreAppState` never falls back to localAppState for these three keys, so a legacy file doesn't inherit the open drawing's pages. A saved viewport for the active page overrides scroll-to-content on load.
decisions.reason: additive, and an older reader ignores it (NFR-1).

decisions.choice: ActionResult gains `replaceDrawing?: boolean`, set by actionLoadScene, loadFileToCanvas and App.initializeScene. When both the old and the new drawing are the one default page, the load takes today's path and stays undoable. Otherwise history is cleared and the store snapshot is reset, so the load is not undoable.
decisions.reason: undo of page structure is out of scope, and a delta can't span pages.

decisions.choice: SCENE_INIT and SCENE_UPDATE gain optional `payload.pages`; MOUSE_LOCATION and USER_VISIBLE_SCENE_BOUNDS gain optional `payload.pageId`. No new WS subtype. A page switch re-sends the last pointer payload and relays bounds so remote cursors and followers update without a pointer move. Everything stays inside the encrypted payload (NFR-6). A collaborator with no `pageId` is an older client and is always shown.
decisions.reason: older clients ignore unknown payload fields, and follow already has a channel.

decisions.choice: The scene document keeps `sceneVersion`, `iv` and `ciphertext` as today, where `ciphertext` still decrypts to an element array, and gains `pagesIv` and `pagesCiphertext`. The page list is encrypted with the room key. Firestore `update` leaves the new fields alone when an older client writes the document. firebase-project rules need no change (`allow write: if true`).
rejected: Changing `ciphertext` to `{elements, pages}`: an older client's `restoreElements` would crash on it
decisions.reason: older clients keep reading rooms, and page names stay encrypted.

decisions.choice: AppPages commits with flushSync, so `api.createPage()` followed by `api.setActivePage(id)` reads the new list. The search flow, which starts in a useEffect, defers its switch with queueMicrotask because flushSync can't run inside an effect.
decisions.reason: React batches setState, and page ids must be usable by the very next call.

decisions.choice: One component, PageTabs.tsx, with plain markup: role tablist/tab, roving tabindex, HTML5 drag events, and a small role=menu popover closed by useOutsideClick and Escape. Page operations call `app.pages` directly; they are not actions and have no command-palette entries. Delete confirmation uses ConfirmDialog.
rejected: DropdownMenu: its trigger always adds class `dropdown-menu-button`, which test-utils and interactivity tests query as the main menu
Radix Tabs: its triggers fire on mousedown and can't host the rename input
An action per operation: five files of wiring for no shortcut the requirements ask for
decisions.reason: same file set, works in jsdom, and meets NFR-5.

decisions.choice: Rendered by LayerUI once, for every form factor, after the form-factor blocks and outside `.footer-center` and `.layer-ui__wrapper__footer`, centered above the footer, with data-viewport-ui="bottom". Hidden when `defaultUIEnabled` is false, when `appState.zenModeEnabled` is true, or when `UIOptions.pageTabs === false`.
decisions.reason: `.footer-center` belongs to the host, its inline snapshot must not change, and view mode on phones has no bottom bar to live in (FR-12).

decisions.choice: `exportScene` filters `data.elements` with `getActivePageElements(data.elements, data.appState)` when `data.appState.activePageId` is set. Embedded scene data goes through `scopeAppStateToActivePage`, which leaves one page record and one viewport. A host exporting a non-active page passes `appState: { activePageId }`.
decisions.reason: FR-18 also holds when a host passes onChange's elements straight to exportScene.

decisions.choice: JSONExportDialog receives the whole drawing's non-deleted elements from LayerUI, and the Excalidraw+ and share call sites in excalidraw-app pass the same. ImageExportDialog keeps the active page's elements.
decisions.reason: FR-28 carries all pages, while FR-18 scopes images.

decisions.choice: LocalData and localStorage.ts need no change: onChange gives them every page and the three AppState keys are browser:true. Tab sync passes `pages` through `restorePages` to updateScene, and each browser tab keeps its own active page (FR-3); when the stored active page differs, the stored scrollX, scrollY and zoom are not applied.
decisions.reason: FR-23 with no new storage key, and legacy records load through restore.

decisions.choice: Exactly three snapshot files change, because they dump full appState: history, regressionTests and contextmenu. Each is regenerated by its own tooling unit after the code is in. Nothing in element snapshots changes because default-page elements carry no `pageId`. The diff of each must hold only `activePageId`, `pageViewports` and `pages` keys (NFR-9). packages/utils/tests/__snapshots__/utils.test.ts.snap and packages/excalidraw/tests/packages/__snapshots__/utils.test.ts.snap have no test file and stay untouched.
decisions.reason: a generator owns these files; typing them would be 133 identical hunks.

units.behaviour: The page model as pure functions: element membership, the page list and its edits, reconciliation, and the helpers save and export use.
rules: No App, React or AppState import. Functions taking appState declare the structural fields they read. Depends only on @excalidraw/common, @excalidraw/fractional-indexing, ./mutateElement and ./types.
Order: a private comparator sorts by index, then id. getLivePages filters `isDeleted` and sorts; it returns a new array.
getElementPageId returns `element.pageId ?? DEFAULT_PAGE_ID`.

adoptElementsIntoPage mutates in place and returns the same array. For each element whose getElementPageId differs from pageId, or whose pageId equals DEFAULT_PAGE_ID: when pageId is DEFAULT_PAGE_ID delete the `pageId` key, otherwise assign it. It does not bump version: the caller owns these elements. Cast through Mutable.
groupElementsByPage returns a Map from page id to elements, keeping each group's array order and first-seen key order.
hasPagedElements is true when any element has a truthy pageId. It is the fast-path test for restore and reconcile.

getDefaultPage returns a new record {id: DEFAULT_PAGE_ID, name: `${PAGE_NAME_PREFIX} 1`, index "a0", version 1, versionNonce 0, isDeleted false, updated 0}. It uses no random or clock value, so it is identical across clients and snapshots.
getNextPageName looks at live names only and matches them against /^Page (\d+)$/ built from PAGE_NAME_PREFIX. N is one more than the highest match, or 1 when none matches (FR-5).
normalizePageName trims, slices to MAX_PAGE_NAME_LENGTH, and returns `fallback` when the result is empty (FR-5). Duplicate names are allowed.
A private bumpPage returns `{...page, ...updates, version: page.version + 1, versionNonce: randomInteger(), updated: getUpdatedTimestamp()}`.

newPage returns a record with id randomId(), the normalized name (fallback getNextPageName(pages)), index `generateNKeysBetween(last live index or null, null, 1)[0]`, version 1, versionNonce randomInteger(), isDeleted false, updated getUpdatedTimestamp(). It does not add the record to the list.
renamePage bumps the record when the normalized name differs and returns `pages` unchanged otherwise. An empty name keeps the previous name (FR-5).

movePage: `toPosition` is the target position in the live order, clamped to the range. Take the live list without the page, and generate an index between the neighbours at toPosition. When the neighbours have equal indices, reassign every live page's index with generateNKeysBetween(null, null, n) in the target order and bump each record whose index changed. Return `pages` unchanged when the position does not change.
deletePage bumps the record with isDeleted true. It does not check the last-page rule: that belongs to the caller.

getNeighbourPageId takes the live pages in order, a page id, and an optional set of ids still live. It returns the next page in order, else the previous one, skipping ids outside the set, or null when none exists (FR-10, FR-27).
getPagesVersion sums `version` over all records including tombstones.

reconcilePages merges by id. When only one side has the pristine default record (id DEFAULT_PAGE_ID, version 1) and the other side is non-empty, drop it. For an id on both sides: if either is deleted the result is the deleted record with the higher version; otherwise higher version wins, then lower versionNonce, keeping local on a tie. Sort the result. When no live record remains, revive the lowest record with `{...record, isDeleted: false}` and no bump, so all clients revive the same one. Return the `localPages` reference when nothing differs from it.

applyPageTombstones: with no tombstones return `elements` unchanged. Otherwise map elements, replacing each non-deleted element whose getElementPageId is a tombstoned id with newElementWith(element, { isDeleted: true }); return the input reference when none changed.
getActivePageElements returns `elements` unchanged when `appState?.activePageId` is undefined or no element has a pageId and the id is DEFAULT_PAGE_ID; otherwise it filters by getElementPageId.

scopeAppStateToActivePage returns appState unchanged when it has no `pages`; otherwise a copy where `pages` holds only the active record, or the first live record when no record matches, and `pageViewports` comes from getPageViewportsForSave and holds only that page's entry.
getPageViewportsForSave returns `pageViewports` with the active page's entry set to {scrollX, scrollY, zoom: zoom.value} when those fields are present; it returns `pageViewports ?? {}` otherwise.

isValidPageIndex is true for a non-empty string that validateOrderKey accepts, with the throw caught. assignPageIndices returns copies with indices from generateNKeysBetween(null, null, pages.length) in the given order, with no bump; movePage's reindex uses it.

units.behaviour: Restore repairs page data: legacy and malformed input become one default page, elements are restored page by page, and appState's page keys are restored from the supplied data only.
rules: restorePages: a non-array or empty input returns [getDefaultPage()]. Otherwise walk the entries: skip anything that is not an object with a non-empty string `id`, and skip an id already seen (first wins). name is normalizePageName of a string name with fallback getNextPageName(accepted so far). version is a finite number >= 1, else 1. versionNonce and updated are finite numbers, else 0. isDeleted is `!!isDeleted`. Keep tombstones.

restorePages ordering: when every accepted index passes isValidPageIndex and no two are equal, sort live and tombstones together by index then id. Otherwise run assignPageIndices over the accepted records in input order. When no live record remains, return [getDefaultPage()].
restoreActivePageId returns the supplied id when it names a live page, otherwise the first live page's id (FR-21).

restorePageViewports keeps entries whose key names a page in `pages` and whose scrollX, scrollY and zoom are finite, with zoom passed through getNormalizedZoom. Anything else is dropped; a non-object input returns {}.

restoreElementPages returns the input reference when every element's getElementPageId is a page in `pages`, tombstones included. Otherwise it maps: an element on an unknown page, or with no pageId when the default page isn't in the list, becomes a copy on the first live page; a move to DEFAULT_PAGE_ID removes the key. No version bump, like other restore normalization.

restoreElements: run restoreElementPages first when opts.pages is set, so moved elements join the first page's group in array order. When no element has a pageId, call restorePageElements once, so a one-page drawing takes exactly today's path. Otherwise flatMap restorePageElements over groupElementsByPage's groups. One `existingIds` Set is shared across groups, so a duplicate id across pages still gets a new id. Bindings and frames are repaired against one group, which enforces FR-15.
